Date: 2027-09-02 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcela Ortiz (Ozone Head of Data Platforms), Samir Patel (Ozone Security Eng), Elliot Chu (Ozone CTO)
summary: Introductory compliance and key-management discovery. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII-sensitive inference workloads. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO attestations, SSO/SAML + SCIM for RBAC, KMS integration options (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed), audit log retention and schema, and data residency/retention policies. Agreed to share security documentation and schedule a VPC deep-dive.
topics: SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for RBAC
Encryption at rest and KMS options (BYOK/HSM)
Audit logs schema, retention, and SIEM integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data isolation)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Marcela Ortiz: Hi, good thanks. We're excited to understand the security posture for inference — we've got some sensitive meter and customer PII that will be part of prompts.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Thanks Marcela. We usually start with certs and attestations — SOC2 and ISO — and then walk through auth, keys, and logging. Is that the flow you want?
[00:24] Elliot Chu: That sounds right. Quick context: we're doing a phased rollout, first internal tools, then customer-facing alerts. Timeline is end of Q4 for pilot.
[00:33] Samir Patel: I want to jump in on the KMS side — we can't use vendor-managed keys for production because of policy, need BYOK and HSM backed keys. Also retention windows are limited by GDPR and local regs.
[00:45] Jordan Miles: Got it. On SOC2/ISO — Redwood publishes our SOC2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate, we can share the attestation bundle after an NDA. We'll also include our control mappings.
[00:55] Marcela Ortiz: Great. Can you describe how audit logs surface? We need token-level tracing and ability to ship to Splunk.
[01:04] Priya Nair: Yes — logs include per-request metadata: model id, route, token counts, latency, requester id. We support either forwarding logs via an HTTPS collector or forwarding to your SIEM via a syslog connector for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can configure log export to our secure S3 export for compliance.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Is the log schema stable? We run detection rules against field names.
[01:26] Priya Nair: It's mostly stable, but we do versioned schemas. We map fields in the docs and provide a sample event payload — we'll attach that.
[01:35] Elliot Chu: About auth — we need SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC so engineers can't egress data. How granular is RBAC?
[01:45] Jordan Miles: We support role-based permissions at route/model and workspace level. With SAML + SCIM you can map groups to roles; for Dedicated and Private you can enforce network-level policies and restrict model variants.
[01:55] Marcela Ortiz: Does your SAML support IdP-initiated flows and SLO?
[01:59] Priya Nair: Yes, SAML 2.0 with both SP and IdP initiated flows and optional SLO. SCIM v2 provisioning works for user and group sync.
[02:08] Samir Patel: For KMS — can we bring our keys from AWS KMS and have Redwood use them to encrypt model caches and persisted artifacts?
[02:16] Priya Nair: For Private deployments you can BYOK directly — Redwood will call your KMS via customer-managed IAM roles in the VPC. For Dedicated we offer a BYOK option in enterprise plans, and for Hosted we have a Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption; BYOK is available with a contract and dedicated tenancy.
[02:34] Marcela Ortiz: Envelope encryption — does that mean Redwood stores a DEK and wraps with your KMS?
[02:39] Jordan Miles: Exactly, we use a data encryption key per workload and wrap/un-wrap via the KMS. We provide key-rotation logs to customers.
[02:47] Elliot Chu: What about retention and deletion? If we need to delete all generated embeddings or cached KV, what guarantees exist?
[02:55] Priya Nair: We have retention controls per workspace and per-model. For Hosted, we default to 30 days for temporary caches but can configure longer or shorter for enterprise. For Dedicated/Private you control the lifecycle — we can run deletion jobs that zero out caches and purge persisted artifacts; we provide audit evidence. There's a documented deletion API we can call.
[03:15] Marcela Ortiz: Do you support data residency — can inference run entirely in eu-west-1 or on-prem for EU customers?
[03:21] Jordan Miles: Yes — hosted has region pins, Dedicated gives region isolation, and Private can run on-prem or in your VPC region. For strict data residency we recommend Private.
[03:31] Samir Patel: One of our blockers is network egress — for hosted, tokens might leave our network. Can you explain network flow?
[03:38] Priya Nair: Hosted traffic terminates in Redwood's control plane and serving tier; we support private peering and VPC endpoints for eligible plans to eliminate public internet hops. Dedicated provides dedicated GPU pools in a customer VLAN. Private gives you full control.
[03:50] Marcela Ortiz: Latency concerns — our inference calls have to be real-time for some internal dashboards. How do Dedicated and Private compare latency-wise with Hosted?
[03:59] Priya Nair: Dedicated typically matches hosted latency but with more predictable jitter; Private on-prem will be lowest latency if it's colocated with your app tier. We can run a benchmark with a 95th percentile SLA for Dedicated if you need.
[04:12] Elliot Chu: Pricing tradeoffs — is Dedicated much more expensive?
[04:16] Jordan Miles: Dedicated has a committed capacity model — higher base commit but lower per-token cost at scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with slightly higher unit costs. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet with your estimated qps and seq lengths.
[04:29] Samir Patel: Regarding audit — we need immutable audit logs for egress and key access. Do you have WORM or append-only storage?
[04:36] Priya Nair: For Dedicated/Private we can configure append-only buckets and integrate with your key/retention policies. Hosted audit streams are tamper-evident and we can supply export snapshots for audits.
[04:47] Marcela Ortiz: About third-party attestations, do you provide pen-test summaries?
[04:51] Jordan Miles: We publish a summary and can provide redacted pentest reports under NDA.
[04:56] Elliot Chu: Ok, specific technical ask: Samir would like an architecture doc showing how Redwood would mount our KMS and where secrets live in both Dedicated vs Hosted.
[05:06] Samir Patel: Also need to see proof that access to decrypted payloads is restricted. We have to show controls to auditors that no human operator can read customer data without explicit process.
[05:16] Priya Nair: We have technical controls (KMS-based encryption keys and IAM policing) plus operational processes. For Private we don't touch keys. For Dedicated we separate control plane access and have encrypted-at-rest in serving nodes. We'll add a diagram.
[05:27] Marcela Ortiz: Can Redwood provide a demo where we run a synthetic workload with our retention policy and collect logs into our Splunk?
[05:33] Jordan Miles: Yes, that would be part of a pilot. We'll script a workload and forward logs to your Splunk instance.
[05:40] Elliot Chu: What's the fastest way to get to a pilot while satisfying compliance? We don't want a months-long procurement.
[05:45] Jordan Miles: A scoped pilot on Dedicated with strict network controls can start in 4-6 weeks given procurement. Private takes longer because of on-prem install. We'll also support a limited-hosted pilot with enterprise contracts and BYOK if procurement prefers speed.
[05:58] Samir Patel: Any blockers about encryption algorithms — we need AES-256-GCM and KMS that supports RSA/ECC for signing.
[06:06] Priya Nair: We support industry standard ciphers, TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-GCM for at-rest and standard signing. We'll list cipher suites in the security pack.
[06:15] Marcela Ortiz: On data deletion proof, do you provide signed deletion receipts?
[06:20] Jordan Miles: We can generate signed audit records for deletion operations showing key wrap/unwrap operations and timestamps.
[06:28] Marcela Ortiz: Ok great. A few quick questions from our legal: indemnity boundaries when you run models that might output customer-sensitive derivations. How does Redwood approach liability?
[06:40] Jordan Miles: Legal can handle standard vendor indemnity. For model outputs we recommend guardrails and we can discuss an indemnity carve-out; we'll involve our legal counsel in the next stage.
[06:49] Elliot Chu: Anything else on compliance?
[06:52] Samir Patel: One more — retention policy for logs, longer retention for audit trails vs short retention for caches. We need separate retention classes.
[06:59] Priya Nair: We support tiered retention: ephemeral caches (24-90 days), long-term audit (configurable 7+ years) for enterprise. We'll provide retention configs.
[07:10] Jordan Miles: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs, attach log schema and sample payloads, supply a VPC/private checklist, and schedule a VPC deep dive for next week.
[07:20] Marcela Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:23] Elliot Chu: Thanks, bye.
[07:25] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[07:27] Priya Nair: Bye all.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (some technical acronyms transcribed inconsistently). Links shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf (to be sent post-call).
